card.name: Emotional news stories of violence and loss
card.fires_on: Scattered words (pronouns like my/her/us, children, million, punctuation) inside emotionally heavy general-web stories about killing, abuse, genocide, drowning, or suffering. It follows the grim subject matter, not one specific word.

modes.label: Violence and atrocity
modes.description: Words inside accounts of murder, rape, or genocide, such as a possessive or a victim group.
modes.example: six million innocent Jewish men, women and<< children>> were murdered, just because they were Jews

modes.label: Personal family tragedy
modes.description: Pronouns or punctuation in stories about a child or relative in danger or distress.
modes.example: never thought she would hear these words from<< her>> seven-year-old son, Brian, but

modes.label: Social grievance essays
modes.description: Pronouns or sentence starts in opinion pieces on cultural harm or bullying.

card.writes: Weak and mixed; it promotes Chinese demonstratives like 这一/这项 and suppresses words like 'always' and 'ever', so there is no clear effect on the output.
card.plain: It lights up on ordinary words in serious, upsetting news stories about violence, loss, or hardship.
